summary: Preserved candidate PR 2371's eager cross-stream event ordering and corrected its host-thread race by holding a per-communicator lock across guard bookkeeping and the native legacy/V2 enqueue. The candidate still cannot fully resolve the original issue because concurrent CUDA graph replay bypasses Python and both native implementations retain unbounded device spins.

tests.what_was_measured: Exact candidate 39673680441fb67c3934e0139f317742a2aa4353 lacks a lock spanning the legacy and V2 native launches.
Corrected source holds stream_guard.serialize() around both native launch paths.
10 tests passed: thread exclusion, eager stream ordering, graph-capture boundary, legacy/V2 launch hooks, and adjacent V2 capability behavior.
On one AMD Instinct MI350X gfx950, two host threads and two GPU streams produced ordered result 2, matching CPU reference 2.

tests.command: pre-commit run --files <changed source, tests, and report files>
tests.what_was_measured: All applicable formatting, lint, spelling, safety, and registered-test registry checks passed.

gpu_execution.evidence: reports/j-e89cf3de41b7/raw/gfx950_host_thread_probe.txt records AMD Instinct MI350X gfx950 and ordered_numeric_result=2 matching cpu_reference=2. This is an ordering primitive test, not the original multi-GPU CUDA reproduction.

remaining_limitations: Only one AMD gfx950 GPU was available; the two-A100 NVLink CUDA deadlock and green-context workload were not reproduced.
Concurrent CUDA graph replay bypasses the Python guard and remains unsafe for graphs sharing one communicator.
V2 push/pull and legacy AOT polling loops remain unbounded; no speculative CUDA device deadline was added without CUDA compiler, ISA, and runtime validation.
No full model or serving workload was run.
